title: Prefix Sums
summary: Build cumulative totals, then answer ranges with two lookups

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: range_sums(values, queries) returns sums for half-open ranges [left, right). Build a prefix table once, then watch each query cancel the part before left.

idea: prefix[i] is the total before i. The extra zero handles ranges beginning at zero and empty ranges. Trace the table being built, then compare the two boundaries for each query.

title: Monotonic Stack
summary: Resolve waiting days as a warmer temperature arrives

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: warmer_days(temperatures) gives the number of days until a strictly warmer day, or zero. Use pending indices to avoid restarting a search for every day.

idea: The pending stack stores indices whose warmer day has not arrived. Each index enters and leaves once. Equal temperatures stay pending because the question asks for a strictly warmer day.

title: Topological Sort
summary: Release tasks as their final prerequisite is removed

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: task_order(graph) returns any valid prerequisite-first order, or None for a cycle. graph maps every node to outgoing neighbours; every neighbour is a key.

idea: Indegree counts prerequisites that remain. Removing a ready task reduces the counts of its dependants. If no task is ready but some remain, a cycle blocks the schedule.

title: 0/1 Knapsack
summary: Fill a capacity table without taking an item twice

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: pack(items, capacity) returns the maximum value of items that fit. Each (weight, value) item may be taken once; weights are positive and values nonnegative.

idea: The table records the best value at each capacity. Iterate capacity downward so each transition reads a state that has not used the current item. Trace upward updates to see why they would solve an unbounded problem instead.

title: Bellman–Ford
summary: Relax weighted edges and detect reachable negative cycles

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: shortest(n, edges, start) returns distances for nodes 0..n-1, using float("inf") for unreachable nodes. Each edge is (from, to, weight). Return None if a negative cycle is reachable from start.

idea: One full pass can extend a shortest route by another edge. A simple path has at most n-1 edges. Any reachable edge that can still improve a distance after those passes proves a reachable negative cycle; an unreachable cycle must not invalidate the result.

title: Edit Distance Rows
summary: Compare prefixes with insertion, deletion and substitution

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: distance(a, b) returns the fewest single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions turning a into b. Keep only the previous row and the current row.

idea: Each cell compares two prefixes. Above means delete, left means insert, and the diagonal means match or substitute. Two rows are enough because older rows are never read again.

title: Linear Regression
summary: Move a fitted line by following the mean squared-error gradient

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: fit(xs, ys, steps, rate) begins at w=b=0 and returns (w, b) after steps of gradient descent on mean squared error. Compute both gradients from the old parameters; include the factor 2/n.

idea: The gradient tells which parameter direction increases loss. Subtracting it moves downhill. Watch the fitted line and loss curve; a large learning rate can overshoot even when the derivatives are correct.

title: Logistic Regression
summary: Turn a score into a probability and learn a binary boundary

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: fit(xs, ys, steps, rate) starts w=b=0 and returns (w, b). Use sigmoid(w*x+b) and gradients mean((p-y)*x), mean(p-y) for binary cross-entropy. Inputs in this lab have moderate scores.

idea: The sigmoid maps a real score into (0,1). For binary cross-entropy its derivative with respect to the score is p-y. The trace shows the parameters and mean squared probability residual as a diagnostic, not as the optimized loss.

title: Nearest Neighbours
summary: Rank points by distance, then vote with explicit tie rules

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: nearest_label(points, labels, query, k) classifies numeric vectors. Equal distances preserve training order; a tied vote chooses the smaller integer label. k is positive and training data is nonempty.

idea: Squared distance has the same ordering as Euclidean distance. The trace keeps distances, selected indices and votes visible. Feature scales change which points are neighbours; stable tie rules make the outcome reproducible.

title: Decision Stumps
summary: Try thresholds and choose the lowest weighted Gini impurity

variants.title: Practice
variants.prompt: best_split(values, labels) returns the midpoint between consecutive distinct sorted values with the lowest weighted Gini impurity. Equal scores choose the smaller threshold. Return None when fewer than two distinct values exist.

idea: A split is useful when it leaves purer groups. Weight each group by its size, then compare candidate midpoints. Scanning thresholds in ascending order and accepting only a lower score gives a deterministic smallest-threshold tie break.
